senses.gloss: A short message posted on a social media site, especially Twitter or X.
examples: His *tweet* got thousands of replies overnight.
She deleted the *tweet* an hour after posting it.
The whole story started with a single *tweet*.

senses.gloss: One of two things that are exactly alike.
examples: This lamp is the *twin* of the one in my office.
She finally found the *twin* of the missing earring.
The new model is a near *twin* of last year's car.

senses.gloss: An unexpected change in a story or a situation.
examples: The movie's *twist* caught everyone off guard.
In a strange *twist*, the thief called the police himself.
The case took another *twist* this week.

senses.gloss: A kind or category of person or thing.
examples: What *type* of car does she drive?
This *type* of soil holds water well.
The store carries three *types* of batteries.

senses.gloss: The kind of person someone finds attractive.
examples: He's nice, but he's not really my *type*.
Tall and quiet has always been her *type*.
You two are exactly each other's *type*.

senses.gloss: Someone or something that is greatly wanted but almost impossible to find.
examples: A quiet, affordable apartment downtown is a *unicorn*.
Candidates with both skills are *unicorns* in this field.
A landlord who returns your deposit is a total *unicorn*.

senses.gloss: The joining of two or more people or things into one, especially a marriage.
examples: Their *union* lasted more than fifty years.
Three children came from that *union*.
The merger created a *union* of two old rivals.

senses.gloss: A group of people forming one part of a larger organization.
examples: His *unit* was stationed in Germany for two years.
She works in the department's research *unit*.
Both *units* report to the same commander.

senses.gloss: A single apartment or home inside a larger building or complex.
examples: The building has forty-eight *units*.
Their *unit* is on the third floor, facing the park.
Two *units* are still available for rent.

senses.gloss: A separate machine or piece of equipment that does one job.
examples: The air conditioning *unit* sits on the roof.
A new heating *unit* runs a few thousand dollars.
The *unit* quit in the middle of the heat wave.

senses.gloss: A new version of a program that fixes problems or adds features.
examples: The phone downloaded an *update* overnight.
This *update* finally fixes the camera bug.
*Updates* install automatically on Tuesday nights.

senses.gloss: A move to a better seat, room, or level of service.
examples: We got a free *upgrade* to first class.
She asked about an *upgrade* to a room with a view.
*Upgrades* go to frequent flyers first.

senses.gloss: A large metal container with a tap, used for serving coffee or tea to a crowd.
examples: There's a coffee *urn* at the back of the hall.
Someone refilled the *urn* before the second service.
The church keeps two *urns* for potluck suppers.

senses.gloss: The amount of something that is used.
examples: Our water *usage* went up in July.
Check your data *usage* before you stream the game.
The app tracks your screen *usage* by the hour.

senses.gloss: A person who regularly takes illegal drugs.
examples: The clinic treats heroin *users*.
Most *users* start in their teens.
He was a *user* for years before he got help.

senses.gloss: The quality of being useful.
examples: The study questions the *utility* of yearly screening.
A second phone has limited *utility*.
They doubted the *utility* of the new rules.

senses.gloss: The electricity, gas, and water supplied to a building, or the bills for them.
examples: Rent is twelve hundred a month plus *utilities*.
*Utilities* run about a hundred fifty in the winter.
Her paycheck barely covers rent and *utilities*.

senses.gloss: A job that has not been filled.
examples: The school has two teaching *vacancies*.
She applied for a *vacancy* in the front office.
The *vacancy* was posted online yesterday.

senses.gloss: A belief about what is right and important, usually used in the plural.
examples: They raised their kids with strong family *values*.
The company's stated *values* include honesty and respect.
We don't agree on much, but we share the same *values*.

senses.gloss: The number or amount that a symbol or measurement stands for.
examples: Solve the equation for the *value* of x.
The sensor reports a *value* between zero and one.
Enter the *values* in the second column.

senses.gloss: A flap inside the heart or a body tube that keeps liquid flowing one way.
examples: He had surgery to replace a heart *valve*.
The *valves* keep blood from flowing backward.
A leaky *valve* showed up on the scan.

senses.gloss: Too much pride in one's looks, abilities, or achievements.
examples: His *vanity* wouldn't let him wear glasses.
The whole building project was an exercise in *vanity*.
She has enough *vanity* to check every mirror she passes.

senses.gloss: A strong locked room where money or valuables are kept.
examples: The bank keeps the gold in an underground *vault*.
The original documents are locked in the *vault*.
Two guards stood outside the *vault* all night.

senses.gloss: A jump over a piece of equipment in gymnastics, or the apparatus itself.
examples: She scored highest on the *vault*.
His second *vault* was nearly perfect.
The *vault* has always been her strongest event.

senses.gloss: A means of expressing, achieving, or spreading something.
examples: The show was really a *vehicle* for her comedy.
Art can be a *vehicle* for protest.
The fund is a *vehicle* for saving on taxes.

senses.gloss: Something that hides the truth or keeps something out of sight.
examples: The deal was made under a *veil* of secrecy.
A *veil* of mist hid the far shore.
He finally lifted the *veil* on how the company operates.

senses.gloss: A layer of mineral or ore running through rock.
examples: Miners followed a *vein* of silver deep into the hill.
The quarry hit a *vein* of white marble.
*Veins* of coal run under the whole valley.

senses.gloss: One of the thin lines that carry liquid through a leaf or an insect's wing.
examples: Hold the leaf up and you can see its *veins*.
The *veins* on a dragonfly's wing form a fine net.
Dark *veins* ran through the pale green leaf.

senses.gloss: A particular style or mood in which something is said or done.
examples: He told another joke in the same *vein*.
The second half of the book continues in a lighter *vein*.
Several speakers went on in that *vein* for an hour.

senses.gloss: Extreme bitterness or hatred in what someone says.
examples: He talked about his old boss with real *venom*.
There was *venom* in her voice.
The letter was three pages of pure *venom*.

senses.gloss: An opinion or judgment reached after trying or examining something.
examples: So what's your *verdict* on the new restaurant?
The critics' *verdict* was harsh.
The *verdict* on the phone is that the battery is weak.

senses.gloss: Someone with long experience in a job or activity.
examples: She's a twenty-year *veteran* of the police force.
The team signed a *veteran* to steady the young players.
He's a *veteran* of three political campaigns.

senses.gloss: One instance of a video or web page being watched or looked at online.
examples: The video hit a million *views* in a day.
Her channel averages five thousand *views* a post.
That clip got more *views* than the whole series.

senses.gloss: An occasion of watching or looking at something, such as a film or an exhibition.
examples: The museum held a private *viewing* for members.
A second *viewing* of the movie showed me details I'd missed.
The gallery scheduled a *viewing* of the new paintings.

senses.gloss: The time when something was made or produced.
examples: The house is of 1920s *vintage*.
He drives a station wagon of recent *vintage*.
Those jokes are of ancient *vintage*.

senses.gloss: Records as a music format, or the records themselves.
examples: He collects old jazz on *vinyl*.
The album came out on *vinyl* and streaming the same day.
Her *vinyl* takes up a whole wall of the living room.

senses.gloss: A bluish purple color.
examples: The sky turned a deep *violet* after sunset.
The rainbow runs from red through blue to *violet*.
She painted the front door a soft *violet*.

senses.gloss: Something seen in a dream or a religious experience.
examples: The saint reported a *vision* of an angel.
He woke from a *vision* of a burning city.
*Visions* of her grandmother came to her during the fever.

senses.gloss: The right or chance to express an opinion and be listened to.
examples: Renters deserve a *voice* in the decision.
The union gives workers a *voice*.
Students had no *voice* in setting the schedule.

senses.gloss: The form of a verb that shows whether the subject acts or is acted on.
examples: Scientists often write in the passive *voice*.
The editor asked her to switch to the active *voice*.
English has two *voices*, active and passive.

senses.gloss: The right to take part in an election.
examples: American women won the *vote* in 1920.
The bill would give sixteen-year-olds the *vote*.
Many citizens were denied the *vote* for decades.

senses.gloss: The votes cast by one group of people, taken together.
examples: The candidate is counting on the young *vote*.
The suburban *vote* decided the race.
He carried the rural *vote* easily.

senses.gloss: A person who takes advantage of other people's troubles for profit.
examples: *Vultures* moved into the neighborhood after the flood, buying homes cheap.
Investors circled the failing company like *vultures*.
He called the payday lenders *vultures*.

senses.gloss: The track of disturbed water left behind a moving boat.
examples: Ducks bobbed in the boat's *wake*.
The skier cut back and forth across the *wake*.
The ferry left a wide *wake* across the bay.

senses.gloss: The period and the conditions that follow an important event.
examples: Thousands lost power in the *wake* of the storm.
In the *wake* of the scandal, two officials resigned.
Rebuilding began in the *wake* of the fire.

senses.gloss: The way a person or animal moves on foot.
examples: I recognized him from across the street by his *walk*.
The horse has an easy, rolling *walk*.
Her *walk* changed after the surgery.

senses.gloss: In baseball, first base awarded to a batter after four balls.
senses.ru: уок (выход на первую базу после четырёх болов)
examples: He drew a *walk* to load the bases.
The pitcher gave up three *walks* in one inning.
A leadoff *walk* often comes back to hurt you.

senses.gloss: A metal frame that a person leans on for support while walking.
examples: She gets around the house with a *walker*.
After the hip surgery he needed a *walker* for a month.
The hallway is wide enough for two *walkers* to pass.

senses.gloss: A person who is walking, especially for exercise.
examples: The trail is popular with *walkers* and runners.
Early-morning *walkers* filled the park.
She's a fast *walker*, so I had trouble keeping up.

senses.gloss: Something that blocks progress or keeps people apart.
examples: The investigators ran into a *wall* of silence.
At mile twenty, runners hit the *wall*.
Years of arguing built a *wall* between them.

senses.gloss: The side or lining of a container, a pipe, or a part of the body.
examples: Fat builds up on the *walls* of the arteries.
The *walls* of the tank are two inches thick.
Acid had eaten through the *wall* of the pipe.

senses.gloss: A long, determined campaign against something considered bad.
examples: The city declared *war* on potholes.
The *war* on drugs has gone on for decades.
The two chains are in a price *war*.

senses.gloss: A district of a city, used for elections and local government.
examples: She represents the Ninth *Ward* on the council.
Each *ward* elects one member.
Turnout was highest in the downtown *ward*.

senses.gloss: A child or adult placed under the legal care of a guardian or a court.
examples: He became a *ward* of the state at nine.
The judge made the twins *wards* of the court.
Her uncle's *ward* inherited the farm.
